title: Sprucehaven retail catalog sync — call + field notes
content:
Context: 11/13 kickoff with Sprucehaven product + infra team. They run a headless retail stack (catalog + search + personalization). Goal: use Redwood for on-demand product description generation, embeddings-based search + rerank, and a daily batch job to refresh embeddings/descriptions for ~1.2M SKUs. Must be private-deploy (VPC) for compliance — PII in product metadata (supplier contacts, pricing tiers).

Attendees: Maya (RWI), Ethan (RWI), Sofia (RWI), Diego (Sprucehaven infra), Maria Gomez (Sprucehaven product), Alex Park (Sprucehaven data), Ravi Iyer (Sprucehaven security).

Immediate asks from customer:
- Low-latency on-demand descriptions for PDP pages (target p95 < 200ms).
- Embedding search for top-k retrieval, then lightweight rerank/generation for personalization.
- Daily batch job to regen embeddings and short descriptions overnight; ability to rescore quickly after morning price updates.
- Single VPC/private deployment with integration to their KMS (AWS KMS) and S3 for catalog assets.
- Audit logs must be retained 90 days; must integrate with their SIEM (Splunk).

Call notes / technical details captured:
- Catalog size: ~1.2M SKUs, daily delta ~8k new/updated. Typical description length source: 30–120 words.
- Images stored in s3://sprucehaven-catalog/images/…; thumbnails used for UI only. No image inference required for MVP.
- SKU id format inconsistent: old SKUs include prefix 'SPC-' and some legacy numeric ids. We need a canonicalization layer before calls to Redwood to avoid cache fragmentation.
- Their current embeddings pipeline uses Faiss on EC2; they prefer Redwood-hosted embedding generation + exporting vectors to their Faiss cluster (for now).
- Throughput: peak 60k read requests/min across global CDN; only ~2% require on-demand generation (profile pages). So main cost is batch regen and embedding generation.

Prelim architecture suggested (sketch):
- Private Redwood control plane in their VPC with Dedicated inference nodes pinned to a quantized LLM for generation (e.g., 3B or 7B variant) for cost balance.
- Short descriptions: generate via batch job using Redwood Optimize config: sequence length cap 256 tokens, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95.
- Embeddings: daily regen in parallel workers; export to s3 in parquet with embedding size 1536.
- On-demand flow: prefix cache for common product templates + KV cache for recently visited SKUs. Use policy: p95 SLO 200ms, fallback to cached short description or old description if generation fails > 250ms.

Gotchas / risks (callouts):
- Cache key explosion due to inconsistent SKU normalization. TODO: normalize to "supplier|sku" format upstream.
- Large nightly batch (1.2M) will stress GPU pool if run cold; recommend staggered batches and autoscale window. Need Dedicated reserved capacity to guarantee overnight throughput.
- Multilingual support: ~12% of catalog descriptions are non-English. Need per-locale generation or language detection pre-step. Batch job should partition by locale.
- Tokenization surprises: many product spec fields include long serial codes and bullet lists which explode token count. For cost predictability, trim spec fields with regex prior to generation.
- Splunk integration: customer expects log events with request_id, sku, model_version, tokens_in/out. Confirm Redwood Console log export shape and ensure field parity.

Cost considerations noted by customer:
- Will accept a mixed approach: embeddings generation + export (affordable) + smaller model for generation on demand. Ask: cost estimate for nightly batch (1.2M embed + 200k short desc) vs. steady-state on-demand.

Action items / next steps (owners + tentative ETA):
- Maya: produce two capacity scenarios (Dedicated reserved vs burst) with cost delta and latency numbers. Due: 2024-11-21.
- Ethan: prototype canonicalization script for SKUs (python) and sample normalized dataset for 10k SKUs. Due: 2024-11-19.
- Sofia: draft batch job orchestration recipe (stagger windows, parallel workers, backoff) and Redwood autoscale knobs required. Due: 2024-11-22.
- Diego (customer): confirm KMS policy and provide test IAM role for staging. Due: 2024-11-18.
- Alex (customer): share sample CSV + 2 weeks of delta exports (anonymized) to s3://redwood-temp/sprucehaven-samples. Due: 2024-11-17.
- Maya/Ethan: schedule 30m follow-up to review sample normalization & first cost sketch. Target: week of 2024-11-25.

Open questions for next call:
1) Do they want generation behind auth (paywall) for some supplier-only descriptions? Affects latency path and cache TTL.
2) Acceptable regeneration cadence for personalized descriptions (per-session vs per-day)? Impacts embedding + rerank frequency.
3) Are there legal restrictions on shipping any derived outputs out of their VPC? If yes, must ensure embeddings never leave their infra.
4) Which model sizes are acceptable for initial rollout (they asked about "fast & cheap" vs "best quality"). We should present a 3B quantized + 7B baseline.

Quick config notes to try in prototype:
- Redwood generation config: model: rwi-3b-quant, max_tokens: 256, temp: 0.2, top_p: 0.95, stop: ['\n\n'], stream: false, kv_cache_ttl: 86400
- Embedding job: batch_size: 2048, embedding_model: rwi-embed-1536, export_format: parquet, incremental_mode: true
- Canary rollout for model upgrades: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error rate > 1.5x baseline

Notes to self (informal):
- avoid pushing full description generation for every UI hit; prefer cached short desc + on-demand long desc async.
- keep sample set anonymized before sharing with internal bench tests.
- double-check Splunk field names with security to ensure PII not logged.

Meeting end: customer keen on speed/cost tradeoff. Next sync scheduled 11/20 9am PT (follow-up to review normalization prototype + initial cost scenarios).

-- Maya
